title: Sort kiwis by squeezing them gently: the ripe ones into the bowl, the hard ones into the paper bag
instruction: Eight kiwis lie in the two trays: four are ripe and four are still hard, and they look the same. Squeeze each one gently in its tray to feel which it is, without crushing it. Then put the ripe kiwis in the white bowl and the hard ones in the paper bag.
context: Squeezing fruit to find the ripe ones is something almost everyone does at the shop or at home, and store staff do it when they pick produce for online orders. Kiwis barely change colour as they ripen, so only a gentle squeeze tells them apart: the robot has to feel about 1 mm of extra give at a few newtons on each of eight kiwis, without crushing the ripe ones.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Two white foam-board pocket trays taped to the table, one each side: a 3 mm floor 17.5 x 15 cm, walls 1 cm tall, dividers 1.5 cm (between rows) and 2 cm (between columns), forming four pockets 7.5 cm (x) by 6 cm, centred at x 23 and 32, y 14 and 22 on the left (L1 near inner, L2 near outer, L3 far inner, L4 far outer) and mirrored on the right (R1-R4). In each pocket lies one green (Hayward) kiwi, 62-72 mm long, 50-54 mm wide, 90-110 g, long axis forward (simulated: 68 x 52 mm, 100 g). Four are ripe (give test: 150-450 g on a kitchen scale at 1.5 mm of pressing, at 20 +/- 3 C) and four hard (2,000 g or more); which four pockets hold the ripe ones is drawn before each trial (70 layouts, TASK_SEED 0-69), and they look alike. A white ceramic serving bowl, 23 cm across the rim, 11 cm across the foot, 8 cm deep, stands centred at (43, 0), fixed with putty. A brown kraft paper bag, size #12 (about 18 x 11.5 cm base), its top rolled down to stand 12 cm tall, open side up, its inside spanning x 4.5-15.9 and y -9 to 9, taped down. Both grippers wear nitrile finger cots (XL, one per finger, mandatory). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. (The right tray's outer pockets look darker in the screenshot: the arm's shadow only.)
scoring: Each kiwi at the end, at rest and let go (no gripper touching): RIGHT if in its own container (ripe: the bowl, centre within 9.5 cm of its axis, below the rim; hard: inside the bag, below its top) AND it was squeezed in its pocket first (both pads of one gripper closed on it for at least 0.5 s before it left the pocket: video, and finger gap at or below its caliper size across the grasp: width, or length if gripped end to end; in simulation each pad at least 1 N) AND, if ripe, never crushed; WRONG if in the other container, squeezed or not; otherwise nothing. A ripe kiwi is crushed if squeezed more than 6 mm below that size (finger-gap log against the size on the trial sheet) or split or leaking juice; in simulation, pressed over 15 N by any robot part. Score = (right - wrong - 4) / 4, clipped to 0-1: 0.25 at right minus wrong 5, 0.5 at 6, 0.75 at 7, 1.0 with all eight right. Doing nothing, or all eight in one container, scores 0; blind guessing averages at most 0.036.
reset_notes: Each session: check the scale with a 500 g calibration weight and the give-test press with a Lee Spring LCM095D14M spring (330 g +/- 10% at one turn); give-test every kiwi (README: kitchen scale under an M10 screw press, one turn = 1.5 mm; ripe 150-450 g, hard 2,000 g or more) at 20 +/- 3 C after 2 h out of the fridge; fit new nitrile finger cots; check each gripper's reported gap on a 50 mm reference with the cots on. Re-test every kiwi hourly or after every 10 trials it was used in, and any dropped kiwi; replace any out of band, split, bruised or crushed; after juice, wipe the fingers and fit new cots. Between trials (2 min): kiwis into two labelled boxes (ripe, hard; never mark the fruit), draw TASK_SEED 0-69 with any RNG, lay them in the pockets it names, and write each kiwi's caliper width and length on the trial sheet by pocket (the squeeze and crush checks use the size across the grasp). Ripe kiwis keep up to 5 days at 0-4 C; sessions last at most 4 h at room temperature.
fidelity: Kiwis are rigid 68 x 52 mm, 100 g ellipsoids with PhysX compliant contacts: ripe 5,000 N/m per contact (about 2 mm of give between two pads at 5 N; about 380 g on the give test), hard 100,000 N/m. Crushing is a rule: a ripe kiwi pressed with over 15 N by any robot part counts as crushed. Real kiwis aren't linear springs; the give test bounds them. Trays, bowl and bag are fixed rigid shapes; the bag's paper is rigid. The finger cots aren't modelled.
scores: Dream-1 (seed 28): 0.0 at the 3,600-step limit. Both grippers shut by 15 s; the right arm (right of video) crept over its tray, its shut gripper hovering 2 cm above and beside the near outer kiwi at 86 s; the left arm (left of video) stayed back. Nothing touched. Demo (seed 28): 1.0 at 43 s.
